item.title: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models design binding proteins without specialized biology models
item.description: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code alone, with 35 of 322 lab-made minibinders binding their intended targets across five targets. (OpenAI)

item.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
item.description: The authors trace long-context training crashes in Gated DeltaNet-2 to an asymmetric erase operation that inflates the recurrent state, and fix it by making erasure symmetric. (Xichong Zhang, Xixuan Hao, Zhichen Liu et al. · MemTensor)

item.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
item.description: A small reasoning model can absorb a stronger teacher's agent policy from the teacher's actions alone, with its own reasoning block left empty during training, and still think at inference. (Dawid J. Kopiczko, Tijmen Blankevoort, Yuki M. Asano · University of Technology Nuremberg, NVIDIA)

item.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
item.description: Letting models decide when and what to compact in their own context beats harness-triggered compaction at tight budgets, but only for models that actually use the interface. (Alessio Devoto, Avinash Vem, Tara Safavi et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
item.description: A memory agent running on separate GPUs prepares text and image memory for the next shot before its prompt arrives, giving a real-time video generator long-term consistency at about 1% extra time. (Shaoteng Liu, Shuai Yang, Wei Huang et al. · NVIDIA, MIT, CUHK)

item.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
item.description: Putting a mirror in the scene cuts success rates of five generalist robot policies by 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points, and most failures happen without the robot ever touching the mirror. (Xuanchen Liu, Hejun Zhang, Boxuan Dong et al. · Peking University)

item.title: Nvidia reportedly halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries after new US chip export rule
item.description: The Financial Times reports that Nvidia told server makers to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after a US rule made advanced-chip exports to those countries subject to licences. (The Star (Reuters), Al Jazeera)

item.title: 42 state attorneys general move to stop bankrupt Character.AI from auctioning users' private chats
item.description: A bipartisan coalition of 42 attorneys general is intervening in Character.AI's bankruptcy to block a 1 December auction of chat histories from more than 21 million US accounts. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
item.description: Plain supervised fine-tuning on the saved rollouts of a reinforcement learning run, in order and without reward labels, reproduces the run's learning curve, and one late batch can recover its final score. (Jiayi Sheng, Jingwen Gu, Guanning Zeng et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Harvard University)

item.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
item.description: The Mixture-of-Loops Transformer passes attention keys and values between loops instead of only the residual stream, so a looped model can decode each new token in a single pass. (Lianghui Zhu, Shijie Wang, Xinggang Wang et al. · Huazhong University of Science & Technology, ByteDance Seed, University of Toronto)

item.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
item.description: OmniAct trains one 400M-parameter manipulation policy on about a million procedurally generated robot arms, feeding it each robot's joint geometry in camera coordinates so it can control bodies it has never seen. (Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Jiayuan Yan et al. · University of Washington, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)

item.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
item.description: Agents often answer while their own stated belief still lists several possibilities; rewarding each step against the simulator's exact posterior teaches them to keep gathering evidence until it settles the answer. (Richmond Sin Jing Xuan, Peilin Feng, Wenbin Wang et al. · Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
item.description: ThinkMorph-SSL turns classic self-supervised image tasks such as jigsaw and denoising into practice for models that reason by generating intermediate images, raising accuracy by 11.33 points across twelve benchmarks. (Jiawei Gu, Linjie Li, Yiming Liu et al. · University of Washington, Tsinghua University, Zhejiang University)

item.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4, a 750B-scale flagship that runs 28 shared layers twice per forward pass
item.description: Chinese lab Z.ai released GLM-5.4, its first flagship built as a looped transformer, available only in its own products for now, with open weights promised after safety hardening. (Z.ai developer docs, Simon Willison, MarkTechPost)

item.title: Anthropic shares fall below their $83 IPO price less than a week after the record listing
item.description: Anthropic's stock dropped below its $83 offer price on Tuesday, trading near $76 at midday, as a broad technology selloff erased the premium from its Nasdaq debut. (The Globe and Mail, TechCrunch)

item.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
item.description: A fine-tuned model can run a multi-step hidden rule entirely in its activations, then write chain-of-thought that justifies the result without mentioning the rule, and a frontier LLM monitor does not flag it. (Tomer Ashuach, Zorik Gekhman, Avi Caciularu et al. · Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Google Research)

item.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
item.description: Judged at equal token cost, agent teams beat independent agents only when they move facts no single agent holds, and such teams can train their successors on their own verified work. (Lixuan He, Shengqu Cai, Fang Wu et al.)

item.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
item.description: Loom attention lets each attention head choose, per token, which earlier heads it reads from, and a 2.8B model built this way matches a 12B Pythia baseline for about 2% extra compute. (Da Xiao, Qingye Meng, Shengping Li et al. · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, ColorfulClouds Technology)

item.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
item.description: VOPD uses the agreement between a verifier and a teacher model on sampled answers to strengthen or reverse the teacher's token-level guidance, giving dense training signal that is tied to checked outcomes. (Juntong Shi, Stefano Ermon, Jure Leskovec et al. · Stanford University, Google DeepMind)

item.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
item.description: A controlled study of how to wrap a frontier multimodal model as a robot policy reaches 83.3% on RoboLab-120 and finds the model succeeds through spatial target estimation, not low-level motion skill. (Xiao-Ming Wu, Kang Liao, Yuexiao Ma et al. · Nanyang Technological University, ACE Robotics, SenseTime Research)

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, with agents that fix pull requests and approve routine code changes
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Ship bundles Code Review with two beta agents: PR Steward, which repairs pull requests, and Claude Approvals, which approves routine changes under a policy the team writes. (The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX, alleging Grok still generates sexualized deepfakes of real people despite safety claims
item.description: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia filed the first state lawsuits against SpaceX over Grok, alleging weak image safeguards and misleading safety statements in violation of consumer protection laws. (The Verge, Ars Technica)

item.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
item.description: Harnesses that keep context outside the model and call sub-models through code can be trained on short tasks and then solve tasks up to 64 times longer, because every individual call stays familiar. (Alex L. Zhang, Souradip Chakraborty, Omar Khattab · MIT CSAIL)

item.title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models
item.description: A second residual stream carried from each token to the next turns a pretrained transformer into a recurrent model with 2,752 new parameters, raising competition-math accuracy and enabling reasoning hidden from the text. (Ziyang Cai, Xingyu Zhu, Sanjeev Arora · Princeton University)

item.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
item.description: OWE-Bench gives agents 26 expert-written engineering tasks lasting hours and scores them on hidden cases, where every model does worse than on the cases it could test against, and worse than it predicts. (Jacob Cole, Martin Dimakis, Victor Barres et al.)

item.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
item.description: RoboThink has a slow reasoning model watch a fast robot policy and pass corrections through a channel the policy is trained to read, recovering from motion drift and misheard requests. (Yunbei Zhang, Zijian Jin, Janet Wang et al. · Tulane University, NYU, Northeastern University)

item.title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
item.description: A 0.8B-parameter model that edits its own weights raises its GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2%, but the authors show it does not understand its edits and random search sometimes does as well. (Guoming Ling, Shanshan Zhong, Kaixuan Zhang et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, MilkThink)

item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared metric for industry limits on AI development, and publishes OpenAI's own numbers
item.description: Jakub Pachocki argues that held-out perplexity should become a cross-lab measure of progress, discloses OpenAI's internal figures, and proposes limits that labs would not cross until monitoring improves. (OpenAI, TechCrunch)

item.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
item.description: Inserting search queries and retrieved passages into ordinary pretraining text teaches small language models to search and to trust evidence, an advantage that later fine-tuning on search data does not fully reproduce. (Kaustubh Ponkshe, Gyung Hyun Je, Stefan Taga et al. · EPFL, University of Toronto)

item.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
item.description: Each RL-trained expert model is distilled into 256 learned input vectors on a frozen base model, and experts combine simply by concatenating those prompts, matching full multi-teacher distillation. (Zhen Zhang, Changyi Yang, Xuehai He et al. · University of California, Santa Barbara, Carnegie Mellon University)

item.title: Neural Geometry as a Learning Signal
item.description: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B only to make an internal representation match its idealized circle or helix, with no loss on outputs, improves task accuracy about as much as ordinary fine-tuning. (Eric Todd, Tal Haklay, Nikhil Prakash et al. · Northeastern University, University of Southern California, University of Amsterdam)

item.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
item.description: BioEmu2 is one diffusion model that predicts biomolecular structures, samples their equilibrium ensembles and jumps forward in time, covering proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and ions far faster than molecular dynamics. (Michael Gastegger, Adam E. Foster, José Jiménez-Luna et al. · Microsoft)

item.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models
item.description: Planning longer with a latent world model can turn working plans into adversarial examples of the model; checking that planned actions can be read back from predicted states largely fixes it. (Huiyuan Tian, Chih-Yung Wen, Shijian Li · Zhejiang University, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

item.title: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims a Lean-formalized proof of the Riemann hypothesis, found working with Claude
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis and formalized it in Lean; outside mathematicians report the code compiles, but no human-readable proof exists yet. (Levent Alpöge, The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: Google rolls out Genie 4, its most realistic interactive world model, to Google AI Ultra subscribers
item.description: Google DeepMind's Genie 4 world model reaches paying users in Project Genie, letting them edit generated worlds mid-session with text prompts and adding real-time native audio. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
item.description: PMD distills diffusion models into four-step generators that keep the teacher's diversity, by matching "tilted" posterior means that each cost a single teacher call at a shifted input. (Hidir Yesiltepe, Julius Berner, Arash Vahdat et al. · Virginia Tech, NVIDIA)

item.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
item.description: Stream of Belief lets several copies of a frozen LLM reason together by exchanging probability-weighted "belief tokens" instead of text, iterating until their joint state stops changing. (Yu Yao, Jiayi Dong, Yilun Du · MIT, UCLA, Harvard)

item.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
item.description: Gamer is a vision-language-action model that plays complex 3D games in real time from raw screen pixels with keyboard and mouse, trained by continued pre-training, sparse-reasoning fine-tuning and long-horizon RL. (Run Luo, Kuan Zhang, Qi Deng et al. · miHoYo, National University of Singapore, Tsinghua University)

item.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
item.description: By deliberately breaking simulated users and checking whether metrics notice, this paper shows existing user-simulator evaluations miss many failures, and proposes a suite that catches all ten tested. (Hengguang Zhou, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen et al.)

item.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
item.description: DNeo, a parallel draft model for speculative decoding, fixes how drafters read the target model's hidden states and remembers rejected drafts, generating up to 1.3 times faster than the previous best. (Jameson Sandler, Shane Bergsma, Mostafa Elhoushi et al.)
